newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Horn says acted quickly in privatisation scandal.
newsitem.headline: Horn says acted quickly in privatisation scandal.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn told a parliamentary panel looking into a 1996 privatisation scandal he acted quickly as soon as he heard about possible illegal payments.

The committee, formed last December, is looking into the so-called "Tocsik affair", in which Marta Tocsik, an adviser to state privatisation agency APV, received 800 million forints ($4.57 million) for negotiating land deals with municipalities on APV's behalf.
The discovery of the payments led Horn to dismiss the entire APV board and the minister in charge of privatisation, Tamas Suchman, last October.

"(The government) ordered a rapid inquiry, the inquiry took five days and then we dismissed APV's board and referred the case to justice," Horn said on Monday in the first case in post-communist Hungary that a prime minister had been called to testify before a investigative parliamentary committee.
Horn told the committee that although he dismissed Suchman because of his political responsibility for the scandal, he was convinced Suchman did not gain from the affair.
"I am convinced that not one penny touched Suchman's hands" he said.
Earlier press reports said part of the success fee paid to Tocsik ended up in the accounts of organisations under the influence of people with close ties to the two ruling parties.

A Budapest court started proceedings in the case in January and, and at the request of Chief Prosecutor Kalman Gyorgyi, Parliament earlier this month lifted the immunity of Laszlo Boldvai, treasurer and MP of the Socialist Party, following evidence that may implicate him in the affair.

Horn earlier said neither the government nor the governing Socialist Party was involved in the privatisation scandal, and noted that the authorities had recovered 600 million forints of the money paid to Tocsik.

Ivan Peto, head of junior coalition partner Free Democrat party (SZDSZ), who also testified on Monday, denied that his party's leaders had any knowledge of illegal payments made to persons with close SZDSZ ties.
"No leading SZDSZ politician had any knowledge of such things," Peto said. ($1=174.99 Forint)
